_doc: Adventure-map encounters (choice events). A map object {type: 'encounter', encounter: <id>} triggers one when a hero walks into it. Each choice may have: requires (conditions, all must hold), cost (resources and/or movement), check (success chance) and outcomes success/failure (or just success when there is no check). Conditions: class, not_class, faction, skill {id: min}, attr {id: min}, army_tag, army_role, min_creatures, terrain (encounter tile), mark, no_mark (persistent hero marks), min_level, min_week, any [conditions]. Effects: resources, xp, recruit, casualties, movement, skill_point, mark, reveal, ambush, artifact, boon {mods, days} (HeroModifiers mods on the hero for days), mana {amount} (restored up to the hero's maximum), veteran_xp {amount} (every stack of the army). sprite (optional): atlas sprite drawn for the encounter, default encounter_<id>. Counts scale with the week via per_week. 'leave: true' keeps the encounter on the map. See src/game/encounter_system.gd.

blessed_by_saint.name: Blessed by the Saint
blessed_by_saint.text: Prayed at a saint's shrine and was answered.

shrine_defiler.name: Shrine Defiler
shrine_defiler.text: Robbed a saint's reliquary. Holy places turn cold.

friend_of_the_road.name: Friend of the Road
friend_of_the_road.text: Carried a dying courier's message. Sellswords and travellers trust you.

pit_champion.name: Pit Champion
pit_champion.text: Won a duel in the ash pit. Fighters respect you.

deathbinder.name: Deathbinder
deathbinder.text: Bound the restless dead of a barrow field.

grove_sworn.name: Grove-Sworn
grove_sworn.text: Swore to spare a sacred grove. The old woods remember.

grove_breaker.name: Grove-Breaker
grove_breaker.text: Felled the ironwood. No grove will speak to you again.

tide_sworn.name: Tide-Sworn
tide_sworn.text: Prayed at the shrine of the low tide. The drowned places open to you.

ashen_saint_shrine.name: Shrine of the Ash-Choked Saint
ashen_saint_shrine.text: A soot-blackened reliquary leans against a dead oak. Inside, a saint's skull still wears a crown of tarnished silver, and the air tastes of old smoke.

success.text: A warmth that is not fire settles over the column. The men march straighter.

failure.text: Only silence answers. The skull's empty sockets watch you go.

success.text: Silver and saint-glass fill your saddlebags. Somewhere, a bell tolls once.

failure.text: Hooded wardens pour from the ruins, howling the saint's name.

dispossessed_column.name: Column of the Dispossessed
dispossessed_column.text: Carts piled with bedding, grandmothers, a goat. Burned-out villagers trudge west, away from the red sky. Their eyes go to your banners, then to the ground.

choices.text: Share provisions and offer them service

success.text: The strongest take up pikes. 'For bread and a roof,' their elder says.
Chains are cheaper than bread.
You see them across the river before dusk. Word of it travels ahead of you.

overturned_wagon.name: Overturned Supply Wagon
overturned_wagon.text: A quartermaster's wagon lies on its side, axle snapped, oxen gone. Crates are still lashed to the bed. The mud around it is churned by too many paws.

success.text: Timber, iron and a paymaster's purse, untouched.

failure.text: The carrion pack that killed the oxen comes back for seconds.

success.text: Your men break up the wagon bed for firewood and stakes.

blind_cartographer.name: The Blind Cartographer
blind_cartographer.text: An old man with milk-white eyes sits among rolled maps, inking coastlines by touch. 'I remember every road,' he says, 'for a price.'

success.text: His charts are uncannily exact.
He trades a scout's tale for a scout's tale, and marks the hidden paths for free.

free_company_camp.name: Free Company Encampment
free_company_camp.text: Tents patched with captured banners. Slingers dice around a fire while their captain, a scarred woman with one ear, sizes up your army.

success.text: Coin changes hands; the company falls in behind you.

choices.text: Negotiate as a friend of the road

success.text: 'I've heard of you,' the captain says. 'Half price, and we keep the loot.'
She yields with a bloody grin. Her company follows the stronger blade.

failure.text: You are beaten in front of both armies. Some of your own desert in the night.

drowned_chapel.name: The Drowned Chapel
drowned_chapel.text: Only the bell tower rises from the black water. Something silver glints in the drowned nave, and the reeds whisper with no wind.

success.text: Your divers surface with quicksilver flasks and gem-set chalices.

failure.text: Something in the black water drags men under. The bell rings, though no one touched it.

success.text: The whispering stops. In the silence you find an offering left on the steps.

barrow_field.name: Field of Unquiet Barrows
barrow_field.text: Grave mounds in rows too straight to be natural, each capped with a rusted helm. The ground is cold even under the sun.

success.text: Grave-gold and burial gems, and nothing stirs.

failure.text: The barrow-cold seeps into the ranks. By morning, some do not wake.

success.text: You speak the old names. The dead grow still and tell you their secrets.

choices.text: Give the field a wide berth

ash_pit_champion.name: Champion of the Ash Pit
ash_pit_champion.text: A fighting pit ringed with spikes and cheering wretches. Its champion, a hulking brute in a branded iron mask, beats his chest at you.

success.text: The mask cracks; the crowd chants your name. Every sellsword between here and the coast will hear of it.

failure.text: You are carried out of the pit. Your purse stays behind, and the day is lost.

success.text: You study the champion's footwork from the rail.

ember_rift.name: Ember Rift
ember_rift.text: The ground splits into a glowing seam. Things with too many joints crawl at its lip, and the brimstone stink makes the horses scream.

success.text: The rift-spawn bow to the ash-brand on your brow and fall in line.
Rock grinds shut over the glow. Brimstone crusts the seam, yours for the taking.

failure.text: The rift vomits its brood before it closes.

thornwolf_den.name: Thornwolf Den
thornwolf_den.text: Bones and bramble mark the mouth of a hollow under the roots. Yellow eyes watch from the dark; the pack has not decided what you are.

success.text: The pack leader takes meat from your hand. The rest follow it.

failure.text: The pack decides you are prey.

success.text: Snarling shapes burst from the smoke.

brigand_toll.name: Brigand Toll
brigand_toll.text: A chain across the bridge, a brazier and a dozen slingers on the far bank. 'Road's ours,' their leader calls. 'Pay up or swim.'

success.text: The chain drops. The brigands melt into the reeds, counting coins.
They take one look at your column and run, leaving their strongbox behind.

failure.text: Their leader calls your bluff.

success.text: Slingstones rattle off your shields.

dying_courier.name: The Dying Courier
dying_courier.text: A rider slumped against a milestone, an arrow through his side and a sealed satchel clutched to his chest. 'The pass at Harrowgate,' he whispers. 'They must know.'

success.text: The garrison pays well for the warning, and the road remembers who brought it.
Coin, a signet ring, and a letter you burn unread.

hall_of_echoes.name: Hall of Echoes
hall_of_echoes.text: A roofless hall where every carved word is repeated back a heartbeat late. Generations of commanders have cut their lessons into its walls.

success.text: Days pass in an afternoon. You leave knowing something you did not before.
The echoes lull the army to sleep. Your scouts rise early and range far.

stranded_salt_caravan.name: Stranded Salt Caravan
stranded_salt_caravan.text: Six wagons of rock salt sit axle-deep in a sinkhole. The drovers have eaten their mules and are starting to eye each other.

success.text: Salt pork and hard biscuit for the whole column. The men march on full bellies.
Your soldiers put their backs into it. The drovers pay what they can and spread your name down the road.

choices.text: Mend the axles with deep-folk craft

success.text: Your smiths have the wagons rolling by noon and take their pay in timber and salt-coin.

bitter_well.name: The Bitter Well
bitter_well.text: A well-house of cracked tile, its rope still wet. The water smells of iron and something older. Someone has scratched 'do not drink' into the lintel, and someone else has scratched it out.

success.text: Cold, clean and strangely heartening. The men sing on the march.

failure.text: By evening the sick are falling out of the line.

success.text: The iron smell fades. Your casters drink deep and feel their strength return.

hedge_witch_hut.name: Hedge-Witch's Hut
hedge_witch_hut.text: A turf hut hung with bird skulls and drying nettles. The old woman inside does not look up from her pot. 'Coin first,' she says, 'questions after.'

success.text: She ties a knot of hair and copper wire to your saddle. Your spells come easier.
She trades a cradle-song for a curse, and both of you come away richer.
The thatch goes up like paper. Something shrieks inside the smoke and comes out swinging.

deserters_fire.name: Deserters' Fire
deserters_fire.text: A dozen crossbowmen in mismatched livery huddle round a fire in a ditch. They have the look of men who ran from the same battle in different directions.

success.text: 'No questions?' 'None.' They stamp out the fire and fall in at the rear.
The ranks watch in silence. Nobody will run from your banner this month.

choices.text: Pretend you did not see them

lost_pilgrims_band.name: Lost Pilgrims
lost_pilgrims_band.text: Barefoot pilgrims in ash-grey robes, searching for a shrine that burned a generation ago. They ask you the way as if you might know.

success.text: They bless every man in the column by name. It takes all afternoon.
Faith is a poor shield, but they will hold a line.

choices.text: Let them walk on after dying

success.text: They find their shrine after all, in a manner of speaking. They do not stop walking.

grey_ferryman.name: The Grey Ferryman
grey_ferryman.text: A flat barge on a rope, and a ferryman with a face like wet clay. 'Across is quicker,' he says. 'Across is always quicker.'

success.text: The barge glides over black water and lands you leagues downstream, fresh as morning.
Your warriors take to the water like coming home. The ferryman nods as if he expected it.
He hands over the fare-box without a word and steps into the river. He does not come up.

failure.text: Things rise from under the barge when he whistles.

abandoned_quarry.name: Abandoned Quarry
abandoned_quarry.text: Terraces of cut stone step down into a flooded pit. Rusted picks still lie where the quarrymen dropped them the day the sky turned red.

success.text: A day of hard labour, and carts full of good grey ore.
Your deep-folk find the vein the surface men missed, and a pocket of crystal below it.
At the bottom of the shaft, a cache of cut gems the last foreman never came back for.

failure.text: Something has been nesting in the shaft.

choices.text: Leave the pit to the water

charcoal_burners.name: Charcoal Burners
charcoal_burners.text: Smoke mounds smoulder among fresh stumps. Soot-black families are felling an old wood one tree at a time and selling the char to anyone with a forge.

success.text: Sacks of char and the yellow crust they scrape from the kilns.
You make them swear by the roots. The wood breathes easier, and so do you.
You pay them to move on. The old wood is quiet, but it noticed.

rune_cairn.name: Rune Cairn
rune_cairn.text: A man-high cairn of flat stones, each cut with angular runes that seem to shift when you look away. The grass around it will not grow.

success.text: The runes are a soldier's prayer, and a map of where the soldier fell.
Under the stones, a hoard of ore-ingots wrapped in rotten leather. The runes go dark.

burned_field_hospital.name: Burned Field Hospital
burned_field_hospital.text: Scorched tents and rows of cots. A handful of wounded soldiers from a lost battle still breathe, tended by a single exhausted surgeon.

success.text: Clean linen and a week's bread. The ones who can walk ask to march with you.
The surgeon flees. You do not stop him. His patients rise and follow you instead.
Tent poles, coin and bandages. The surgeon curses you as you go.

starving_hounds.name: Starving Hounds
starving_hounds.text: A pack of frost-furred war dogs, collars still on, circling the frozen body of their handler. Their ribs show through the fur.

success.text: They eat from your hand and then will not leave your side.

choices.text: Call them in the clan tongue

success.text: Their ears go up at the old words. They know who they belong to now.
Hunger makes them brave.

choices.text: Give the pack a wide berth

smugglers_cove.name: Smugglers' Cove
smugglers_cove.text: Lanterns hooded with sacking, barrels rolled up a shingle beach by night. The smugglers freeze when they see your banners, then decide to smile.

success.text: Quicksilver in sealed jars and brimstone packed in straw, no questions asked.
Smugglers know every path that the patrols do not. Your agents buy all of it.
They scatter into the dark and leave their strongboxes behind.

failure.text: They are better armed than they looked.

old_drillmaster.name: The Old Drillmaster
old_drillmaster.text: A one-legged sergeant on a barrel by the roadside, watching your column march past with open contempt. 'Call that a file?' he says. 'Give me a week.'

choices.text: Pay him to drill the ranks

success.text: Three days of shouting compressed into one. Your veterans grumble and march better for it.
He calls you a fool four times and then teaches you everything he knows.

weeping_spring.name: Weeping Spring
weeping_spring.text: Water runs down the face of a rock carved into a woman's shape, pooling in a basin worn smooth by centuries of hands. It hums faintly with old magic.

success.text: The water tastes of rain and lightning. Your mind clears.
The water settles into quicksilver as it cools in the flasks.
The humming rises to a single clear note. Your column marches as if blessed.

wyrm_carcass.name: Carcass of a Wyrm
wyrm_carcass.text: A wyrm the length of a village lies dead in a scorched furrow it ploughed when it fell. Carrion birds blacken its back. Something else is feeding at the far end.

success.text: Gem-hard scales and crystal from the wyrm's gizzard, before the scavengers notice.

failure.text: The scavengers notice.

success.text: Wyrm-fat burns for a day and a night. Your demons dance in the smoke and come out hungry for war.
The old custom. Every man takes a mouthful, raw and steaming. They will not forget it.

besieged_hamlet.name: Besieged Hamlet
besieged_hamlet.text: Brigands have ringed a walled hamlet and are working a ram on the gate. On the wall, villagers wave torn sheets at your banners.

success.text: The villagers throw their savings down from the wall as you charge.
They take the coin and go. The villagers are grateful, if puzzled.

choices.text: Offer the brigands a better fight

success.text: Their captain knows your name. Half of them change sides on the spot.

sunken_reliquary.name: Sunken Reliquary
sunken_reliquary.text: A reliquary chapel slid into a flooded quarry long ago. Through the green water you can see gilt glinting on the altar, and pale shapes drifting between the pews.

success.text: Your warriors move through the drowned nave as if it were their own temple. Perhaps it once was.
Gold leaf, gem-set candlesticks and a reliquary of crystal.

failure.text: The pale shapes are not fish. Not all the divers come up.

market_of_bones.name: Market of Bones
market_of_bones.text: Stalls of bleached bone and lacquered skulls under a canvas of stitched hides. The traders wear masks and accept any coin, any soul.

success.text: Crates of disassembled dead, packed in salt. Your weavers have them crawling by dusk.
Gems prised from the eye sockets of kings, they say. They are real enough.
The canvas burns, and whatever was trading here is gone by morning.

failure.text: The merchandise objects.

ironwood_grove.name: Ironwood Grove
ironwood_grove.text: Black-barked trees with leaves like beaten copper, ringing faintly in the wind. Their wood turns axes. The air in the grove is very still, and very watchful.

success.text: It takes all day and three broken axes. The timber is worth a fortune. Behind you, the grove goes silent.
The bark splits and wardens step out, stiff with sleep, and fall in beside you.
The ringing leaves lull the army. Wounds close overnight.

cold_forge.name: Cold Forge of the Deep
cold_forge.text: A deep-folk forge-hall cut into the hillside, its great furnace dead for an age. Half-finished constructs stand in rows, waiting for a fire that never came.

success.text: Your smiths sing the old waking-song. The constructs lift their heads.
Ingots, tools and flasks of quicksilver sealed with deep-folk wax.
The fire takes. You temper your army's arms in it before the coal burns out.

failure.text: The furnace takes, and so do the sentinels guarding it.

masked_envoy.name: The Masked Envoy
masked_envoy.text: A palanquin of black lacquer under a silk awning, guarded by slender figures in mirrored masks. A voice from behind the curtain offers to sell you the truth.

success.text: 'Cousin.' The curtain parts a finger's width. A company of knife-dancers bows and joins your train.
Maps, troop counts, the names of traitors. Most of it is even true.
The guards die without a sound. The palanquin is full of gold and sealed letters.

failure.text: The masks were watching for exactly this.

frozen_warband.name: Frozen Warband
frozen_warband.text: A whole raiding party frozen where it camped, rimed men still sitting round a dead fire. One of them blinks.

success.text: Brimstone fires all night. By dawn, a dozen raiders who owe you their lives.
You sing the long song of the clans. Some wake, some do not, and all are honoured.
They stand, still frozen, and do not feel the cold at all.

low_tide_shrine.name: Shrine of the Low Tide
low_tide_shrine.text: When the marsh draws back, a ring of carved stones rises from the mud, each one shaped like a coiled fish. Offerings of shell and bone lie on the central slab.

success.text: The water returns early, warm as blood. Your warriors move like the tide itself.
Something answers. The marsh paths open for you.

failure.text: Something answers. It is hungry.

choices.text: Wait for the water to cover it

brand_sergeant.name: The Brand-Sergeant
brand_sergeant.text: A horned demon in a sergeant's sash sits on a crate of chains beside a glowing brazier. 'Recruiting,' it says, and grins with too many teeth.

success.text: It presses the iron to your standard. Flayers crawl out of the smoke to answer.
Coin buys hounds. The hounds do not ask whose coin.
The sergeant whistles. Its recruits are already here.

tomb_of_the_unbowed.name: Tomb of the Unbowed
tomb_of_the_unbowed.text: A knight's tomb on a hill, the effigy's sword still clasped in stone hands. Fresh flowers lie at its feet, though there is no village for leagues.

success.text: You kneel through the night. In the morning, the column stands straighter.
The stone cracks. What climbs out still remembers its oaths, but not to whom.
Grave-gold and a jewelled scabbard. The flowers wilt as you leave.

failure.text: The knight's sworn dead have not left their post.

giants_toll.name: The Giant's Toll
giants_toll.text: A cairn giant sits across the pass with a boulder in its lap, chewing on a tree. 'Toll,' it rumbles. 'Or song. Or fight. Giant is bored.'

success.text: It shifts aside and points out every path it can see from up there, which is all of them.
A night of mead and boasting. In the morning the giant decides to come along.
It laughs so hard when it falls that the boulder rolls away. 'Good fight!' Every pass in the hills will hear of it.

failure.text: The giant's cousins were sleeping behind the cairn.

stargazers_tower.name: Stargazer's Broken Tower
stargazers_tower.text: A tower snapped off halfway up, its top storey lying in the field like a fallen crown. Brass instruments still turn in the wind, tracking stars no one has seen since the sky went red.

success.text: The charts are older than the kingdoms, and the land has not changed as much as people think.
You understand, briefly, why the sky turned red. The understanding fades; the lesson stays.

plague_cart.name: The Plague Cart
plague_cart.text: A cart heaped with the shrouded dead, its driver slumped over the reins. A bell on the shaft still tolls with every gust of wind.

success.text: The fire burns green. Downwind, a village will never know what you spared it.
The dead were wealthy, once.

failure.text: The sickness was not finished with them, or with you.

success.text: The rats were the real cargo. They follow the bell now.

ember_crucible.name: The Ember Crucible
ember_crucible.text: A ring of slag around a pit of cinders that has not cooled in living memory. A blind tender rakes the coals and says the fire takes one soldier in and gives back what that soldier would have become after a lifetime of war.

success.text: One of your companies walks into the fire singing. What walks out does not sing any more, but it does not need to.

choices.text: Drive them through without the rites

success.text: The coals roar and part. The fire chose them anyway.

failure.text: The fire takes what it is given and gives nothing back.

choices.text: Leave the tender to the coals

barrow_of_the_last_rank.name: Barrow of the Last Rank
barrow_of_the_last_rank.text: A long mound where a whole regiment was buried standing, shields still locked. The shepherds say that whoever keeps the night watch here wakes up with the old regiment's discipline in their bones.

success.text: At dawn one of your companies stands in a line the dead would have recognised. They no longer flinch.

failure.text: The regiment does not like being watched.

success.text: The keepers lead one company down the mound by torchlight. They come back quieter and far more dangerous.

choices.text: Let the dead keep their watch
